news.title: GitLab jumps on Q2 beat, raised guidance
news.summary: GitLab (GTLB) reported Q2 non-GAAP EPS of 24c vs. 18c expected on revenue of $286.25M vs. $273.12M expected, and raised full-year adjusted EPS and revenue guidance. Shares opened up as much as 22-25% premarket and have since decelerated to roughly +10% through midday, with several sell-side price-target increases following the print.

news.title: Dell rallies on FQ2 beat, raised full-year outlook
news.summary: Dell (DELL) beat on both adjusted EPS and revenue for its fiscal Q2 and raised full-year guidance. Shares remain higher by roughly 8-9% through midday, holding most of the premarket gain, with elevated options volume on the name.

news.title: MongoDB slides despite beating estimates
news.summary: MongoDB (MDB) beat Q2 estimates on both earnings and revenue, but shares fell 11-14% after a couple of sell-side price-target cuts -- a guidance-driven pullback rather than a miss on the quarter itself.

news.title: Credo Technology extends post-earnings slide
news.summary: Credo Technology (CRDO) has deepened its decline through the session, now down roughly 20-21% following its Q1 earnings report -- worse than the initial 8-10% premarket drop, not a recovery.

news.title: Iran conflict still live, but Wednesday's tape has firmed further
news.summary: The Iran/Strait of Hormuz conflict that hit markets Tuesday remains unresolved, and the 10-year Treasury yield touched its highest level in roughly a year (around 4.81%) -- but Wednesday's session has kept firming rather than fading, with major indexes broadly higher on the day. Elevated yields remain the more direct drag on equities than the Iran headlines themselves.

news.title: ADP employment out; factory orders and Fed Beige Book still on deck
news.summary: Wednesday's ADP August private-payrolls report has already been released. July factory orders and the Federal Reserve's Beige Book are still scheduled later today. None are policy decisions on their own, but they're today's scheduled data points ahead of Friday's nonfarm payrolls.

news.title: Bitcoin and Ether continue to soften through the session
news.summary: BTC and ETH both traded lower through Wednesday's session (BTC -0.1%, ETH -0.7%, SOL -0.8% vs. today's open); the crypto-proxy equity basket (MSTR, COIN, CRCL, and others) is tracking roughly in line with spot rather than diverging, unlike Tuesday evening's gap.
